definition: Dated mild pejorative for a woman perceived as sexually promiscuous or cheaply provocative.
notes: Softer than 'slut'; connotes tackiness and availability equally; peak use in mid-20th-century American media; now used mostly ironically or humorously.

definition: Archaic pejorative for a prostitute or woman regarded as sexually immoral.
notes: Strong biblical and literary pedigree (KJV, Shakespeare); archaism softens the sting for modern readers; still deployed in religious rhetoric.

definition: A seductive, morally corrupt woman; from the biblical queen; historically weaponized as a racialized stereotype applied disproportionately to Black women.
notes: The 'Jezebel stereotype' is a documented racialized trope in American history used to justify sexual exploitation of enslaved and Black women; the racial dimension is analytically significant.

definition: Archaic term for a prostitute or sexually immoral woman.
notes: Heavy Shakespearean usage; today sounds almost comically theatrical; occasionally repurposed for comic or camp effect.

definition: Archaic adjective or noun for a sexually licentious or dissolute woman.
notes: Has non-sexual senses (wanton cruelty, wanton destruction) that keep the word in passive recognition; the sexual sense is effectively archaic in everyday speech.

definition: Archaic pejorative for a sexually promiscuous or slovenly woman.
notes: Connotations blend sexual looseness with general slovenliness; more common in British than American English; has a theatrical, almost pantomime-villain quality today.

definition: Dated US slang for a woman easily persuaded into sex, from the image of someone whose heels round off so she tips over backward easily.
notes: Effectively dead slang; recognizable mainly to older Americans or slang historians; the physical metaphor (tipping over) makes the submissive posture explicit.

definition: In sexual contexts, a person — typically a woman — who can easily be persuaded to have sex; primary meaning is simply 'easily manipulated person.'
notes: The sexual sense is strongly secondary to the general meaning; low crude score reflects the dominant non-sexual register; inclusion is contextual rather than inherent.

definition: Crude slang for a sexually promiscuous woman in a community, implying she is ridden by everyone.
notes: The vehicle metaphor ('everyone gets a ride') is the rhetorical core; 'town pump,' 'town mattress,' and 'community mattress' are structural variants on the same template.

definition: Crude slang for a sexually promiscuous woman in a community, implying communal access like a public water pump.
notes: Less common variant of 'town bicycle'; the shared-public-resource metaphor carries the same dehumanizing logic; more dated and regional than 'town bicycle.'

definition: Crude slang reducing a sexually available woman to a piece of furniture used for sex.
notes: Object-reduction metaphor; 'community mattress' is an extended form; the furniture comparison is explicitly dehumanizing; recognition of the sexual sense may be higher among men.

definition: Crude slang for a sexually promiscuous woman, from the expression 'everyone gets a turn,' as with a doorknob.
notes: Rarer than 'town bicycle'; the 'everybody gets a turn' logic is typically spelled out explicitly when the term is used; sometimes deployed as an explanatory joke.

definition: Very crude US pejorative for an extremely promiscuous woman, framing her as a low-value prostitute.
notes: The dollar figure signals contempt through cheapness, compounding the shame; 'two-bit whore' is a variant; also used hyperbolically in non-sexual idioms ('spending money like a two-dollar whore').

definition: Crude slang that reduces a person, typically a woman, to a sexual object; most common in the compound 'piece of ass.'
notes: Overwhelmingly woman-directed in practice; can be applied to men but rarely is; the fragmentation implied by 'piece' (not the whole person) makes the dehumanization structural.

definition: Slang for a sexual partner evaluated by performance ('a good lay'), or for the act of sex itself.
notes: Dual noun/verb usage; objectifying but mild enough to appear in mainstream fiction without shock; applies to any gender in principle though historically more often woman-directed.

definition: A person treated as a prize won through seduction; the act of seducing that person framed as a military or competitive victory.
notes: The military metaphor (sex as territorial victory) is so naturalized it is often used without irony; primarily masculine in framing; the partner is cast as passive territory.

definition: A sexual partner counted as a tally in a personal history of conquests, as in 'notch on the bedpost.'
notes: Metonymic shorthand for the full phrase 'notch on the bedpost'; the counting/scorekeeping frame makes the objectification structurally explicit; primarily masculine usage.

definition: A late-night contact made to someone purely for casual sex; also used for the person being contacted in this way.
notes: Emerged from 1990s African-American vernacular; fully mainstream by early 2000s; can objectify the person being called or describe the arrangement neutrally depending on context.

definition: A man admired for his virility and success in attracting or bedding many women.
notes: Derived directly from the male breeding-animal sense; connotation is strongly positive or neutral; the contrast with all-negative female equivalents is a primary data point for gendered shame asymmetry.

definition: A man who skillfully pursues and maintains sexual relationships with multiple women, often with tactical self-awareness.
notes: Mainstreamed through 1990s hip-hop; 'player' implies calculated skill and 'game' rather than mere promiscuity; frequently self-applied with pride; less morally weighted than 'womanizer.'

definition: A seductive, unscrupulous man who pursues women for sexual conquest; from the villain in Nicholas Rowe's 1703 play 'The Fair Penitent.'
notes: Literary origin; connotes rakish charm alongside moral callousness; today mainly used in formal writing or with ironic distance; recognition declining as literary literacy falls.

definition: A man who is a prolific and skilled seducer of women; eponymous from Giacomo Casanova (1725–1798).
notes: Carries connotations of sophistication and romantic talent rather than mere promiscuity; used admiringly at least as often as critically; far less stigmatized than any female counterpart — key data for shame asymmetry.

definition: A man who habitually pursues and seduces many women.
notes: Mildly pejorative but socially far less damaging than female equivalents like 'slut'; the asymmetry in condemnation between this term and its female-coded counterparts is a core signal for cross-cultural shame measurement.

definition: A man so attractive or charming that women find him irresistible; implies great success in seduction.
notes: Overwhelmingly positive in connotation; the violence metaphor ('killer') is fully domesticated; emphasizes appearance and charisma more than promiscuity per se; gender-reversed 'mankiller' exists but is rare.

definition: A promiscuous man, framed pejoratively by borrowing the female-coded shame term 'whore.'
notes: The compound deliberately transfers a feminine shame term to a man; the social damage is measurably lighter than calling a woman a slut, demonstrating that the transfer is imperfect — shame vocabulary is not gender-neutral even when lexically transposed; peak in mid-2000s internet and tabloid usage.
